purpose: Cash-in STRUCTURE metadata (which units make a cash-in, and the board's A* aggregate rule). Structure is official Pearson documentation; every boundary VALUE still comes exclusively from the sha256-recorded grade-boundary documents in raw/.

sources.title: Pearson Qualifications Information Manual 2025/26 — International Advanced A Level section (unit requirements per cash-in code)
sources.usedFor: XMA01/YMA01/YFM01 unit compositions incl. the five allowed YMA01 applied pairs

sources.title: Pearson — International Advanced Level results explained for students
sources.usedFor: A* rule: grade A overall AND at least 90% of the A2 UMS; Mathematics: 480 overall + at least 180/200 from P3+P4; six-unit IALs: 480 overall + at least 270/300 at A2; four-unit IALs: 320 + 180/200

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Science (Double Award) (Modular) specification (2024), 'Qualification at a glance'
sources.usedFor: 4XSD1 = Biology Units 1-2 (4WSD1, 4WSD2) + Chemistry Units 3-4 (4WSD3, 4WSD4) + Physics Units 5-6 (4WSD5, 4WSD6); modular cash-ins are graded on aggregated UMS

sources.title: Pearson International GCSE Modular grade-boundary documents (raw/pearson-int-gcse-modular) — 'Maximum marks and grade boundaries for the overall qualification (the cash-in) are only shown in UMS marks'
sources.usedFor: Modular cash-in grades are UMS-aggregated; unit raw marks convert to UMS through the unit's own published raw+UMS boundary pairs

roadmap.YFM01: Further Maths cash-ins are multi-route (F1 + one of F2/F3 + four of seven applied, OR F1+F2+F3 + three of seven) with cross-cash-in unit locking — encode with the Maths cash-in only after a verified official worked example; display-only until then.
roadmap.bestCombination: Pearson cash-ins use the candidate's best valid unit combination across attempts; this wave's calculator grades the marks the user enters (one mark per unit slot), not a best-of search.
